jobs.name: murakumo inference maturity
jobs.prompt:
One iteration = one landed increment. Do not attempt the whole backlog in a run.
Pick the highest-value item still open, do it end to end, land it, and report what you could not verify.

## Measured picture (2026-09-07). Read before choosing.

`murakumo-main` is served by gad:8090. The unit there is named
`murakumo-ring.service` and its unit file defines a ten-participant RPC ring,
but a drop-in (`murakumo-ring.service.d/qwen38.conf`) blanks `ExecStart=` and
substitutes a **single-node Vulkan server** (`-c 524288 --parallel 2
--spec-type ngram-cache,ngram-simple`). No `--rpc`. The nine RPC workers listen
on `:50052` with **zero connections**. Read effective units with
`systemctl show -p ExecStart`, never `systemctl cat | head`.

Pool, measured from `/slots` and `/v1/models`: gad 2 slots x 262,144 ·
b70 2 x 16,384 · xavier 1 x 8,192. Decode spread is about 7x across them and is
content-dependent (both fast heads run `--spec-type ngram`, so speculative
acceptance moves the rate). Prefix reuse already works — `n_prompt_tokens_cache`
in `/slots` reports the *current* task and reads 0 when idle; the per-request
field is `timings.cache_n` / `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`.

## Backlog, priority order

1. **`cloud-murakumo-api` main is ahead of production by one commit that cannot
   be deployed as-is.** `984c426` fixed a self-contradiction in the published
   capacity document (the `max-concurrency` method text still called b70 one
   slot of 32,768 while `capacity-members` said two of 16,384). Deploy fails
   closed at `scripts/package-release.mjs`: it asserts the committed
   `release/cljs/manifest.json` sourceDigest matches `src/`, and any source
   change invalidates it. **Refreshing the artifact was attempted and abandoned**
   — rebuilding with `clojure -Sdeps '{:deps {thheller/shadow-cljs {:mvn/version
   "2.28.20"}}}' -M -m shadow.cljs.devtools.cli release worker ui` produced a
   bundle differing from the committed one starting at **byte 91** (`ba=` vs
   `ca=`), i.e. globally different minifier symbol assignment, not the +108
   bytes of the intended string. So the artifact could not be attributed to the
   source change and was not shipped. **That is itself the finding**: a gate
   whose purpose is reproducibility is not reproducible on this machine. Work
   out which toolchain produced the committed artifact (compare against the
   `build: refresh governed release artifact` commits) and either restore
   reproducibility or record why it cannot be. Until then this repo cannot be
   deployed at all without an unverifiable artifact.

2. **Publish endpoints the fleet already serves.** Measured on b70:
   `/v1/completions` (400 on empty body = reachable), `/tokenize` (200),
   `/detokenize` (200), `/infill` (500 = reachable), `/apply-template` (400).
   Through `api.murakumo.cloud` all are **404**. `/v1/rerank` and
   `/v1/embeddings` answer 501 on b70 (not started with those capabilities; gad
   runs a separate `murakumo-embed.service`). Exposing the reachable five is
   API-surface parity with vLLM/SGLang at no model cost. Auth, metering and
   admission must apply exactly as for `/v1/chat/completions`. Blocked behind
   item 1 for deployment.

3. **Affinity's counterfactual is unverified.** Cache-aware placement landed
   (`01ade03`, `c10c481`) and is observable via `x-murakumo-affinity`, but the
   demonstration that affinity keeps a request on a *demoted* head could not be
   run because gad was saturated throughout. Also unverified: gad's idle decode
   rate and its prefill rate — every sample was under contention, and no prefill
   is published for gad rather than publishing queueing under a rate's name.

4. **Reconcile the two b70 decode measurements.** Journal timings over 24 h of
   real traffic gave 47.8–49.4 tok/s; deliberate probes gave 16.8 (unpredictable
   content) to 28.2 (predictable). Speculative decoding makes decode
   content-dependent, which is a plausible explanation and was **not isolated**.
   A published decode rate that moves 3x with content needs either a stated
   content class or a bracket.

5. **Drain `verify-capability-provider-status` findings**, one at a time:
   `nbb --classpath ".:scripts/nbb_compat" scripts/verify-capability-provider-status.cljs ~/github/com-junkawasaki --findings`
   Largest group is `inconsistent` between `kototama/src/kototama/browser.cljc`
   and `kotoba-lang/lang/host-parity.edn` about the same host/op pair. Decide
   which table is right by reading the implementation, fix the wrong one, say how.

6. **`capability-llm-infer` still declares `:contract-only`.** The provider
   landed in `kotoba-lang/kotoba` (`868f3fb`) and is now reachable from a mesh
   guest end to end (`kotoba-lang/mesh` `02cf0c67`). Update the declaration to
   what is measured and name which hosts it covers.

7. **Nothing has actually moved onto the mesh yet.** `murakumo.app.edn` still
   keeps the itonami agent's Bot turns off-mesh, correctly — being unblocked is
   not being migrated. Moving one turn and measuring it is the next step, and
   only then does that comment change.

## How to work

Read `~/github/com-junkawasaki/CLAUDE.md` first. Child repos
under `orgs/<org>/<repo>` have a remote named after the **org**, not `origin`,
and their checkouts are often behind — branch from `<remote>/main` explicitly.
Never rebase, never force-push, never write to `main`; land via
`gh api repos/<org>/<repo>/merges`. Fleet hosts are read-only unless the item
says otherwise; an unreachable host is UNVERIFIED, never zero capacity.
If an item is already done, say so with the evidence and move on.
